title: Tunable DNA binding on graphene oxide via polyethyleneimine topology and density: mechanistic insights for nonviral gene delivery.
authors: Davoudinia, Samira; Imani, Rana; Tafazzoli-Shadpour, Mohammad; Fani, Najmeh; Makki, Hesam
one_liner_zh: 该文通过全原子MD模拟研究PEI修饰氧化石墨烯与DNA的结合机制，虽非TF-DNA体系，但聚焦蛋白-DNA互作中的DNA吸附与界面动态，方法可迁移至TF-DNA结合建模。
abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) functionalized with polyethyleneimine (PEI) is a promising platform for nonviral gene delivery, yet the effects of polymer architecture and surface density on DNA binding remain poorly understood. Here, we use extensive all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, including free energy calculations, to elucidate how the topology (linear vs. branched) and grafting density of PEI govern DNA adsorption on GO surfaces. By systematically varying the nitrogen-to-phosphate (N/P) ratio through adjustments in surface amine density, we study the direct impact of this parameter between DNA and GO-PEI interactions. In contrast to common understanding, our potential of mean force (PMF) analysis reveals a non-monotonic relationship between PEI coverage and DNA binding affinity, with intermediate densities yielding the strongest yet reversible interactions. This behavior results from a balance between favorable electrostatic and hydrogen bonding interactions and opposing steric and electrostatic repulsion, amplified by ionic screening at higher densities. Radial distribution function (RDF) analysis confirms the formation of dense chloride ion shells at high PEI densities, which inhibit DNA approach by neutralizing surface charge. We also show that topology plays a key role: branched PEI engages DNA more effectively through multivalent interactions within the grooves, while linear PEI binds more diffusely along the phosphate backbone. These mechanistic insights highlight the critical role of polymer structure and coverage in modulating DNA binding, offering design principles for optimizing GO-based gene delivery systems.
abstract_zh: 聚乙烯亚胺（PEI）功能化的氧化石墨烯（GO）是非病毒基因递送的有前景平台，然而聚合物架构和表面密度对DNA结合的影响仍知之甚少。在此，我们利用广泛的全原子分子动力学（MD）模拟，包括自由能计算，来阐明拓扑结构（线性与支化）及接枝密度如何调控DNA在GO表面的吸附。通过系统改变表面胺密度来调整氮磷比（N/P），我们研究了该参数对DNA与GO-PEI相互作用的直接影响。与常见理解相反，我们的平均力势（PMF）分析揭示了PEI覆盖度与DNA结合亲和力之间的非单调关系，其中中等密度产生最强但可逆的相互作用。这种行为源于有利的静电和氢键相互作用与不利的空间位阻和静电排斥之间的平衡，并在较高密度下因离子屏蔽效应而增强。径向分布函数（RDF）分析证实，在高PEI密度下形成了致密的氯离子壳层，通过中和表面电荷抑制DNA接近。我们还表明，拓扑结构起关键作用：支化PEI通过沟槽内的多价相互作用更有效地结合DNA，而线性PEI则沿磷酸骨架更弥散地结合。这些机制性见解突显了聚合物结构和覆盖度在调控DNA结合中的关键作用，为优化基于GO的基因递送系统提供了设计原则。
